findings.title: 1. BLOCKING — Missing broker record fails open
findings.body: loadBrokerSession returns null for missing or unreadable broker.json, including a possible partial read during its in-place write. Here null becomes an empty exclusion list. If the live shared broker is a child of the worker, cancel can kill the broker and its app-server subtree, disrupting other jobs. This depends on a degraded or concurrent record read, but the code does not establish that null means no broker exists.
findings.recommendation: Write broker.json atomically and refuse a brokered worker kill when its broker identity cannot be established.

findings.title: 2. BLOCKING — Cancel can succeed without a verified kill
findings.body: handleCancel runs the reaper, then awaits turn/interrupt before attempting the kill. If the worker exits in that interval, the kill returns process-missing and alive is false; this branch returns pending:false, so the caller records cancelled and removes PID state although descendants may still be running. The existing dead-root test covers death before the reaper, not this interval.
findings.recommendation: After the interrupt, reconcile a vanished worker as failed or unknown; require verified whole-tree delivery before recording Windows cancellation.

findings.title: 3. SHOULD-FIX — README promises a retry that may not occur
findings.body: The README says SessionEnd will re-judge an unknown worker kill at the next SessionEnd. cleanupSessionJobs initially keeps that job, but activeWorkspaceJobs immediately runs the reaper; if the root died while a child survived, it marks the job failed and clears its PID identity. No later SessionEnd retries that survivor.
findings.recommendation: State that a dead-root survivor is only reported and logged, and may lose its retryable job record in the same SessionEnd.

storedJob.rendered:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

DO-NOT-SHIP: Windows cancellation can kill a shared broker when its record is unreadable, or report success when no worker tree was killed. This was a static review; Windows E2E was not rerun.

Findings:
- [high] 1. BLOCKING — Missing broker record fails open (plugins/codex/scripts/codex-companion.mjs:1346-1352)
  loadBrokerSession returns null for missing or unreadable broker.json, including a possible partial read during its in-place write. Here null becomes an empty exclusion list. If the live shared broker is a child of the worker, cancel can kill the broker and its app-server subtree, disrupting other jobs. This depends on a degraded or concurrent record read, but the code does not establish that null means no broker exists.
  Recommendation: Write broker.json atomically and refuse a brokered worker kill when its broker identity cannot be established.
- [high] 2. BLOCKING — Cancel can succeed without a verified kill (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/job-control.mjs:331-334)
  handleCancel runs the reaper, then awaits turn/interrupt before attempting the kill. If the worker exits in that interval, the kill returns process-missing and alive is false; this branch returns pending:false, so the caller records cancelled and removes PID state although descendants may still be running. The existing dead-root test covers death before the reaper, not this interval.
  Recommendation: After the interrupt, reconcile a vanished worker as failed or unknown; require verified whole-tree delivery before recording Windows cancellation.
- [medium] 3. SHOULD-FIX — README promises a retry that may not occur (README.md:392)
  The README says SessionEnd will re-judge an unknown worker kill at the next SessionEnd. cleanupSessionJobs initially keeps that job, but activeWorkspaceJobs immediately runs the reaper; if the root died while a child survived, it marks the job failed and clears its PID identity. No later SessionEnd retries that survivor.
  Recommendation: State that a dead-root survivor is only reported and logged, and may lose its retryable job record in the same SessionEnd.

Next steps:
- Fix both blocking state transitions, correct the README claim, then rerun the Windows cancel and SessionEnd E2E gates.
